newsitem.title: USA: Plains sees output up at new LA-area field.
newsitem.headline: Plains sees output up at new LA-area field.

text.p: Plains Resources Inc expects to increase oil production by 25 percent this year at its newly aquired Montebello field in the Los Angeles basin, a top Plains exective told analysts Wednesday.
Plains, an independent energy company, bought the field from Chevron Corp last March. The Montebello field has 24 million barrels of oil equivalent.

"We expect to increase production from 800 to 1,000 barrels per day this year alone in improvements to equipment," Plains Chief Financial Officer Phillip Kramer told analysts at an American Stock Exchange energy conference.
Kramer also said the field has 60 proved undeveloped drilling locations with 150,000 barrels of oil per well.
Kramer said the company is eyeing more aquisitions of oilfields in Texas and California.
"We are very pro-active in the acquisition phase. We are looking at opportunities particularly in the San Joaquin Valley."
Plains produces oil out of fields in the Los Angeles basin, South Florida Basin, and the Illinois Basin.
In 1996, Plains produced 6.4 million barrels of oil equivalent, a 33 percent increase over 1995 production.
